title: Surajkund Mela Rides
statement:
India's one of the most prominent and much-awaited Surajkund Mela in Haryana has started. Ninja and his 'K' friends are going to this carnival. This carnival has 'N' amusement rides lined up, and each ride's starting and finishing time is given on the visiting card: [startTime, endTime].

What is the maximum total number of rides the friends can take if they act optimally?

A person can attend at most one ride at a time, and becomes free immediately at t = endTime, meaning they can attend another ride that starts at or after endTime.
inputFormat:
The first line contains T, the number of test cases.
For each test case:
The first line contains two integers N and K.
The next N lines each contain two integers, startTime and endTime of a ride.
outputFormat: For each testcase, print the maximum number of rides the friends can take.

sampleCases.explanation: N = 3 and K = 2, and the [startTime, endTime] of the 3 rides are [1,2], [2,3], [2,5]. The 2 friends can attend all 3 rides: Friend 1 attends ride [1,2] at t = 1; Friend 2 attends ride [2,3] at t = 2; Friend 1 is free at t = 2 and now attends ride [2,5] at t = 2.

N = 4 and K = 2, and the rides are [2,12], [0,3], [1,2], [2,4]. The 2 friends can attend 3 rides: Friend 1 attends ride [0,3] at t = 0; Friend 2 attends ride [1,2] at t = 1; Friend 2 is free at t = 2 and now attends ride [2,4] at t = 2.
